title: A field-valued point in the image of a closed immersion factors through it
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $K$ be a field, and let $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ be a morphism whose unique image point is $i(z)$ for some $z\in Z$. Then there is exactly one morphism $s':\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ with $i\circ s'=s$, and the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ maps to $z$ under $s'.$

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction: a morphism from a reduced scheme factors through a closed subscheme iff it does so set-theoretically), applied to Spec K; Definition Tag 01HK (closed immersion) and Lemma Tag 01L7 (immersions are monomorphisms) give uniqueness

proof.text: *Setup.* Let $\xi$ be the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $x=s(\xi)=i(z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], $s=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s:\kappa(x)\to K$ the field map induced by $s$, where $j_y:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$ denotes the canonical morphism at a point $y$ of a scheme $Y$; and $s\mapsto(s(\xi),\varphi_s)$ is a bijection from morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ to pairs (point, field map), with inverse $(y,\psi)\mapsto j_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)$. Let $r:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ be the map induced by $i$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]; it is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso].

source.place: Schemes, the discussion of morphisms from spectra of fields before Lemma Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points)

proof.text: *Existence.* Put $\psi=\varphi\circ r^{-1}:\kappa(z)\to K$ and $s'=j_z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi):\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to $g=i$ and the point $z$, $i\circ j_z=j_{x}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}$ is a contravariant functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $i\circ s'=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi\circ r)=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)=s$.

source.place: Schemes, the commutative diagram $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ after Lemma Tag 01J9

proof.text: *The point of any lift.* Let $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ satisfy $i\circ u=s$. Then $i(u(\xi))=s(\xi)=i(z)$. A closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its image [def-weil-closed-immersion], in particular injective on points, so $u(\xi)=z$.

source.place: Schemes, Definition Tag 01HK (closed immersion of locally ringed spaces: homeomorphism onto a closed subset)

proof.text: *Uniqueness.* A closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] is a monomorphism (Stacks Tag 01L7). Mathlib supplies this directly: the IsClosedImmersion instance gives IsPreimmersion, whose instance gives Mono i (Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean and Morphisms/Preimmersion.lean). For two lifts u and s' with u ≫ i = s = s' ≫ i, cancel_mono i gives u = s'. No second application of the point-and-field-map correspondence is needed.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms); Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Preimmersion, Mono instance for IsPreimmersion, followed by categorical cancellation

proof_origin.place: The point-and-field-map description before and after Lemma Tag 01J9 gives existence using the residue-field isomorphism of a closed immersion and residue-field point naturality. Uniqueness now uses Lemma Tag 01L7 via Mathlib's Mono instance for preimmersions, instead of repeating the field-map correspondence. The point of every lift follows from injectivity on points. Formalized by P2; the unit route is unchanged.
